records.issue_text: Email send failure is swallowed with console.log only, error object discarded and user still sees success toast (addGuests.handler.ts:170-172)
records.rationale: The diff shows `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` in addGuests.handler.ts — the caught error is discarded and the handler still returns `{ message: "Guests added" }`, so the mutation succeeds and the client shows `showToast(t("guests_added"), "success")` even when guest emails failed to send. This silently masks a partial failure.

records.issue_text: Error toast does t(err.message), which renders raw strings for non-key messages and shows raw error codes via err.data?.code to end users (AddGuestsDialog.tsx:38)
records.rationale: The diff shows `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` — the raw tRPC error code (e.g. 'BAD_REQUEST') is concatenated and shown to the user, and t(err.message) will return the literal untranslated message for non-translation-key errors (e.g. Prisma errors). This is a real minor UX/correctness defect in newly added code; typical handlers in the repo display translated human-friendly messages.

records.rationale: The diff shows the EmailField is fully controlled: `value={field}` with `onChange` updating the parent array via setValue, so when an item is removed mid-list, every re-render passes the correct (shifted) array values to the inputs at each index. Since the displayed value is a prop, not internal state, index-based keys cannot cause stale input values; at most it could cause focus/selection quirks, not the 'stale input state' defect claimed.
